Tennis

Jannik Sinner announces end to his 2026 season because of knee injury - 'I need to think about my long-term career'

By Pete Sharland
Updated 06/10/2026 at 10:49 GMT+1
TNT Sports on Google
React to this story

World No. 1 Jannik Sinner has announced that he is ending his 2026 season owing to injury. Sinner confirmed the news on social media on Tuesday and will now focus on getting back to full fitness for the 2027 season.

Djokovic feels 'sorry' for Medvedev after 'shock' disqualification

Video credit: SNTV

That means the Italian will not be able to defend his title at the season-ending ATP Finals in Turin and he could lose his place at the top of the world rankings.
His absence opens the door for Alexander Zverev and Carlos Alcaraz to battle for the year-end world No.1 spot. 
Zverev is currently ranked world No.2 after his French Open and US Open triumphs, while Alcaraz has dropped to world No.3 as he continues his return from a wrist injury that saw him pull out of the French Open and Wimbledon.
ATP Shanghai

Sinner withdraws from Shanghai Masters – when could he make comeback?

03/10/2026 at 14:48
"Me, together with the doctors, have decided that I need a course of treatment for my knee, which means that the 2026 season is officially over," Sinner said in a video posted on Instagram.
"The last couple of years, especially the ending in Turin, gave me so many beautiful feelings and emotions. This year is going to be way different. But at the moment I also need to think about my long-term career.
"I will do everything possible to get back to 100%. I thank you already in advance for you support, and hope to see you very, very soon on the court."
The world No.1 has been sidelined since defending his Wimbledon title against Alexander Zverev in July.
The five-time Grand Slam champion has had to withdraw from three ATP Masters 1000 tournaments and the US Open since his SW19 triumph. 
Sinner withdrew from the Shanghai Masters, the penultimate ATP Masters 1000 event of the year, on Saturday, but at the time gave no indication that his season was over. He had also withdrawn from the ongoing China Open, an ATP 500 event where he was the defending champion.
  • Why Swiatek was 'really p*****' during Vekic comeback - 'I was just angry'
  • Alcaraz admits to 'struggling' despite reaching Tokyo final
After being thrashed by Alcaraz in the 2025 US Open final, Sinner found a new lease of life, winning the Paris Masters and ATP Tour Finals. 
Despite a semi-final loss to Novak Djokovic in the Australian Open, Sinner further entrenched his position as world No.1, winning five consecutive Masters 1000 titles while compiling a 30-match win streak. 
The Italian’s run ended in an illness-induced loss to Argentina’s Juan Manuel Cerundolo at the French Open, but Sinner recovered to win Wimbledon.
